Choosing a Watering Schedule for Indoor Plants

Contents

  1. Why schedules fail

Why fixed schedules fail

A calendar reminder does not know how much light the plant got this week, so a fixed interval either drowns the plant in winter or starves it in July. The interval has to follow the soil, not the diary.

Read the soil, not the calendar

Push a finger two centimetres into the pot. If it comes out dry, water. If it comes out cool and damp, wait another day and check again.

Light and season change everything

The same pot on the same windowsill needs water twice as often in midsummer as it does in midwinter, because the plant is transpiring more and the compost is drying faster.

Pots without drainage

Avoid them.

Summary

Check the soil, adjust with the season, and let the pot drain. That is the whole method, and it survives contact with a real windowsill.
